title: Pierre du Moulin the father: this fiducia is commanded and to be sought — weak sight still sees the way
source_text: XXXV. Quin celeberrimus Petrus Molinaeus istius Petri Molinaei pater, ante filium idem hac in parte docuit; nam postquam pluribus egit de illa persuasione qua quis promissionem Evangelii sibi applicat, credens peccata sibi per Christum esse remissa, sequentia verba subjungit, Nec tamen haec eo pertinent, ut albo fidelium expungantur, quotquot hunc fidei gradum nondum sunt assecuti, quam Deus non dat omnibus eodem tempore, nec mensura. Sed ut doceamur hanc fiduciam a Deo juberi, & ab eo obnixe petendam esse, & toto conatu in id incumbendum, ut precibus & bonis operibus roboretur & crescat. Adde quod in prima fide, sed non simulata, fumi est locus, etiam lippientibus oculis cernitur via. Nec qui a serpentis aenei aspectu sanabantur pariter erant perspicaces. Fide justif. part. 2. Thesi 39.
pass_a_gloss: Indeed the most celebrated Peter du Moulin, father of that Peter du Moulin, taught the same in this part before his son; for after he treated at length of that persuasion by which someone applies the Gospel promise to himself, believing sins to have been remitted to him through Christ, he subjoins the following words: Nor yet do these things tend to this, that there be struck from the roll of the faithful as many as have not yet attained this degree of faith, which God does not give to all at the same time, nor by the same measure. But that we may be taught that this trust is commanded by God, and is to be earnestly sought from Him, and that we must press with whole endeavor that it be strengthened and grow by prayers and good works. Add that in first faith, but not feigned, there is room for smoke — even with bleared eyes the way is seen. Nor were those who were healed by looking at the bronze serpent equally sharp-sighted. On Justifying Faith, part 2, Thesis 39.
pass_b_english: Pierre du Moulin the father taught the same before his son.
Those not yet at this degree of fiducia are not struck from the roll of the faithful.
God does not give that degree to all at once or in the same measure.
It is commanded, to be sought, and grown by prayer and good works.
First unfeigned faith may be smoky — bleared eyes still see the way (bronze serpent).
